blocks.text:
Jason Vasquez
General Manager
Davis and Sons
Dear Jason,

Thank you for choosing us to lead your search for a Head of Operations at Davis and Sons. This letter sets down the terms of that engagement, so that everything between us is plain from the start. We treat a retained search as a partnership, and we like to begin by putting the whole of it in writing. Please read what follows with care. If a single line does not match what we agreed, call me before you sign.
The Search We Will Run for You

You are looking for a Head of Operations who can take hold of the daily running of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} and give you the room to lead. Our work is to find that person, to test them fully, and to bring you a short slate you can act on with confidence. We run the search on a retained basis. That means we work only for you on this mandate, and we give it our full attention until the seat is filled. Discretion sits underneath all of it. We describe the people we approach by their current role and record, never by name, in anything that leaves our office, and we hold every name in confidence until both sides are ready to meet.
The assignment moves through a few clear stages. I want you to know their shape before we begin, so that nothing about the work comes as a surprise.

items: First, we agree the position specification with you, so that we are all searching for the same person.
Second, we map the market for that person, build a considered long list, and approach each prospect with care.
Third, we interview and assess in depth, then bring you a short slate described by fit and evidence rather than by name alone.
Fourth, we stay beside you through your own interviews, the references, and the offer, and we do not step back until your Head of Operations has accepted and started.

blocks.text: The People Who Will Look After You

I will hold the engagement myself and remain your point of contact for as long as you want one. James Grant, one of our senior consultants, will lead the assignment day to day. He works the market at the most senior level, and his judgment on finalists is as sound as any I know. Nicole Donovan, our research associate, will build the candidate profiles and keep every thread moving, so that nothing on the search goes quiet on you. You will find all three of us easy to reach, and easy to talk plainly with.
Our Fee, and When We Start

For a retained search of this kind we work to a fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}}, which covers the assignment in full, from the specification through to a completed placement. The fee is settled at the outset and does not move as the search moves. It is not tied to the pay of the person we place. You know the cost of the work from the first day. We are ready to begin on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}, once this letter is signed and returned, and we will hold that date open for you.
The rest of this letter sets out the standard terms on which we work. None of it should surprise you. I would still ask you to read it in full, so that we start on the same page.
Fees and Payment

We bill the fixed fee in three parts, each tied to a milestone: on your signing of this letter, on delivery of the short slate, and on your chosen candidate's acceptance of an offer. Our invoices are due on receipt. Reasonable direct costs that we arrange at your request, such as candidate travel, are billed to you at cost and shown in full. We clear anything out of the ordinary with you before we commit to it.
Term and Termination

The engagement runs from the day you sign until the search is done and our final invoice is settled. Either of us may end it earlier, in writing. We ask only for a short conversation first, so that nothing ends on a misunderstanding. If you close the search early for a reason unrelated to our work, we bill for the stage in hand and no more. If a Head of Operations we place leaves you within the first year for a reason within our control, we will reopen the search once at no further fee.
Confidentiality

We treat all that you share with us, and all that we learn along the way, as confidential, and we use it only for this search. Inside our office, only the people named above and those whose work requires it will see it. We extend the same care to the candidates. We do not disclose a prospect's interest to anyone outside your side of the table without their knowledge, and we describe them by their role until you are ready to meet. Discretion is not a courtesy in our trade. It is the reason good people are willing to talk to us at all.
Limitation of Liability

We give the search our best professional judgment. The choice of whom to hire is finally yours, and we cannot warrant how any person will perform once in the seat. Our liability to you under this engagement, whether put in contract or in negligence, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, save in the case of our own fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Should any dispute arise, we will each make a genuine effort to settle it in conversation before either of us looks to another forum.

If these terms read as we agreed, please sign both copies below, keep one for your file, and send the other back to me. That one step is all we need to begin. If anything here gives you pause, call me first, and we will settle it before you sign. We are glad to be doing this with you, Jason, and we mean to do it well.
With warm regards,
Kickoff Memo: Head of Operations Search for Davis and Sons

To: Nicole Donovan
From: James Grant
Re: How we will run the Head of Operations search

Our charge on this assignment is straightforward to state and demanding to execute well, which is to place a Head of Operations at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} whom their General Manager will be glad to have hired a year from now. We confirmed the engagement with Jason Vasquez, the General Manager at Davis and Sons, and we begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}, so before either of us makes a first approach I want the two of us aligned on the objective, on who owns which part of the search, and on the moves we make first. The mandate is a retained search for an operator who can hold the daily running of a business at this scale, not a caretaker of a going concern, and the discretion the firm is known for applies from the outset, which means we describe every prospect by their current seat and record and hold their names close until both sides want to meet.

The specification is not yet written, and settling it with Jason Vasquez is the first real task, but the shape of the role is already clear from what the client has told us, which is that Davis and Sons wants a Head of Operations who has run the operating core of a business of this size, who can bring order to reporting and process without smothering the place, and who will be a genuine partner to the General Manager rather than a deputy who waits to be told. We are searching, in other words, for judgment and drive in equal measure, and the market for that profile is not large, so the mapping has to be careful and the outreach patient.
How the assignment breaks down

items: Specification and calibration: I will draft the position specification and settle it with Jason Vasquez, so that we search against one agreed brief and not two private ones.

Market map and long list: I will lead the mapping at the senior-operator level, working the sectors where a Head of Operations of this profile is actually found, and building the long list from that map rather than from any list we already hold.

Research and candidate profiles: Nicole Donovan will build the tight profiles we circulate, framing each prospect by role and record, and will keep every candidate thread current so that no promising conversation goes quiet while we are busy elsewhere.

Client contact and logistics: I will hold the relationship with Jason Vasquez directly, and we will keep the paperwork and the scheduling orderly so that our attention stays on the candidates and on the client.

blocks.text: Where we begin

Because the specification gates everything that follows, that is where the work starts, and I will have a first draft of it in front of Jason Vasquez within the week so that we are not sitting idle while the client reads. Nicole, once that draft is with the client, please open the market map in parallel and begin assembling the research bench, and set a standing check-in for the two of us so that nothing on the search waits on a calendar. If you see a reason the plan above will not hold, tell me now, before the search is underway, so that we fix it while it is still cheap to fix.
Hello Jason,

A short note on where the Head of Operations search stands before the weekend, so that you have the shape of it in hand. Since we agreed the specification, we have been mapping the market for the role at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}, working the sectors where an operator of this profile is actually found, and the long list is coming together well. Nicole Donovan has begun the first candidate profiles, each drawn by current role and record rather than by name, so that nothing about a prospect's interest in the seat travels before it should.

There is one thing I would ask of you before we go further, which is a short read from your side on two priorities in the specification, so that I am not sending the team against a brief that has quietly shifted since we last spoke. So that discretion holds on the search, I would also suggest that we route every candidate document to you, Jason Vasquez, as the single point of contact at Davis and Sons, and I will keep the thread orderly from our end.

I remain your day-to-day contact on this, James Grant, with Nicole Donovan on the research bench, and I will send you a proposed date for our first review of the field as soon as the long list is closed. Ten minutes by phone works if that is easier than writing the two priorities out.
Regards
Meeting Minutes: Head of Operations Search for Davis and Sons

The team met to review the completed market map for the Head of Operations search at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} and to agree which prospects move into first-round interviews. The map is finished. Interviews of the leading prospects begin next week.
Present

items: Jason Vasquez, General Manager, Davis and Sons

blocks.text: The market map and the field

James Grant presented the completed map. It covers the sectors agreed at kickoff and yields a long list of prospects across them. The field is strongest in the two sectors nearest the client's own and thinner in the third.

Prospects were discussed by current role and record, not by name, in keeping with the firm's practice while a search is live. James Grant walked the list one sector at a time. No prospect was set aside for any reason other than a weaker fit against the specification.
The team then worked through which prospects advance. Fit against the agreed specification was the only test applied. The thinner third sector was left open in case a late name surfaces.

From the long list the team agreed a shortened group to carry into the first round. Outreach to that group has begun. Several prospects have confirmed their interest in a first conversation, and the rest will be approached over the coming week.
Assessment and the next stage

James Grant will take the first-round interviews of the most senior prospects himself, given his experience with senior-operator mandates. Nicole Donovan will hold the candidate threads current while the round runs and finish the profiles the client will see. The two will compare read-outs before any name goes to the client.
The client will see nothing until the field has been interviewed. Names stay in confidence until both sides are ready to meet. This holds for every prospect on the list.
What the client asked for

Jason Vasquez set out how Davis and Sons wants the process run from here. He asked for a short slate rather than a long one, for each candidate to be presented by evidence of what they have built, and for the room to meet finalists without the timetable forcing a decision. The team confirmed the approach already matches those preferences.
Action items

rows: Begin first-round interviews with the leading prospects and record read-outs for the team
Complete the candidate profiles for the shortlisted prospects and keep the threads current
Continue outreach to the remaining shortlisted prospects and confirm their interviews
Confirm who at Davis and Sons will sit on the client interview panel
Propose a date for the next joint review once the first-round read-outs are in

blocks.text: The first round of interviews governs the schedule from here. The team will reconvene with the client once the read-outs are in hand. Names stay in confidence in the meantime.
Status Report: Head of Operations Search for Davis and Sons
Prepared by James Grant, Senior Consultant, for the leadership of Davis and Sons on the Head of Operations search for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}.
Where the search stands

The search is on schedule and now at its midpoint. The market has been mapped, the first round of interviews is complete, a strong group of prospects has emerged, and the work ahead is to narrow that group to the short slate your side will meet. We are working within the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}} agreed at the outset, which covers the assignment in full, and the engagement remains on budget and on time.
What we have done this period

Since the last report the team has closed the market map and moved the search into interviews, which is the point at which a retained search stops being a matter of names on a page and becomes a matter of judgment about people. I have led the first-round interviews of the most senior prospects myself and recorded read-outs for the team, and that first pass has already thinned the field to the operators who genuinely fit what {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} needs of a Head of Operations rather than those who merely look the part on paper.

Nicole Donovan has built the candidate profiles that sit behind each interview, framing every prospect by current role and record, and has kept the candidate threads current so that no promising conversation has cooled while the round has run. Her profiles are close enough to final that they will drop into the slate summary with little further work, which keeps the search moving at the pace the assignment needs.

The specification we settled at the start has held steady through the period, which has kept the search orderly and the team calibrated against a single brief, and we have measured every prospect against it at each step so that the field we are building genuinely answers what Davis and Sons set out to hire. Throughout, we have held to the discretion the assignment demands: prospective candidates have been discussed only by their current role and record, none has been named in anything that circulates, and no candidate's interest in the seat has traveled beyond the few people who need to know it.
What comes next

Over the coming weeks the team will complete the remaining first-round interviews, test the strongest prospects more deeply against the specification, and assemble the short slate for your review, and each candidate on that slate will come to you described by the evidence of what they have built and by their fit with the operating core of the business. We will hold every name in confidence until both sides are ready to meet, which is the discretion that lets people in current seats talk to us at all. Once your side has met the slate, we will move with you into references and stay beside you through to an accepted offer, so that our work ends at the placement and not at the introduction.
Risks and how we are holding them

Two risks are worth naming, and neither is pressing. The first is timing on the candidates' side, because the strongest prospects for a role of this kind are people who are not looking to move, and one or two may need longer to decide than a fixed schedule would prefer, which we manage by keeping them warm and honest about where they stand rather than forcing a pace that would lose them. The second is the depth of the field in one of the three market sectors, which came in thinner than the other two, and which we have covered by weighting the outreach toward the sectors where a Head of Operations of this profile is more likely to be found. Nothing about the cost or the timetable of the engagement has changed since we began, and the search remains firmly within the fee we agreed.

The search is healthy, the field is real, and we are on course to bring you a slate you can act on with confidence. The one thing I need from your side now is a provisional date to meet that slate, which I will confirm the moment the field is firm.
Meeting Minutes: Head of Operations Search for Davis and Sons

The team met with the client to review references on the leading finalist for the Head of Operations search at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} and to agree the final steps to an offer. The references are complete. The client is ready to move to an offer.
Present

items: Jason Vasquez, General Manager, Davis and Sons

blocks.text: References and the finalist
James Grant presented the reference findings on the finalist. The references were consistent and strong. Nothing in them gave the client pause.

The finalist emerged from the short slate the client met in the prior stage. Two candidates were carried to the end. The second remains a strong operator and will be thanked and kept warm in case the offer does not close.

The finalist was discussed by current role and record, as every prospect has been throughout the search. The client confirmed the finalist matches the specification agreed at the start. No open question remained on fit.

The reference conversations covered direct reports, a former supervisor, and a peer from the candidate's current seat. Each was reached with the candidate's consent. The team read back the substance of each conversation without naming the referees.
The client's decision

Jason Vasquez confirmed that Davis and Sons is ready to extend an offer to the finalist. He asked the team to manage the offer and the candidate's transition with the discretion the search has kept throughout. The team agreed to handle the approach and to hold the candidate's name in confidence until the offer is accepted.

The team reviewed the shape of the offer with the client, so that the terms are settled before they reach the candidate. The compensation range was confirmed against what the search set out at the start. The client will put the final terms in writing, and the team will carry them to the finalist.
Transition and start

The team reviewed the steps between an accepted offer and a first day. Nicole Donovan will assemble the placement file and the documentation the client keeps for its records. James Grant will stay close to the finalist through the notice period so that nothing unsettles the move.
The client asked that the transition stay quiet until the finalist has resigned the current seat. The team agreed. No announcement goes out before the candidate is ready.
Action items

rows: Prepare the offer terms with the client and open the offer conversation with the finalist
Finalize the placement file and the candidate documentation for the client
Confirm the offer terms and the intended start date with Davis and Sons leadership

blocks.text: The offer is the last step in the search. The team will confirm the placement with the client once the finalist has accepted.
